entry.content:
CLAE revisits the classic '70s plimsoll with the Nelson, a minimalist low-top that trades nostalgia for clean lines and considered materials. This White and Off-White edition pairs premium Nappa milled leather with a rubberized toe cap for a refined finish that still feels ready for everyday wear. Underfoot, a custom-molded footbed made with 80% recycled PU foam teams with CLAE's Standard Premium sole, combining natural rubber and a hidden EVA insert for lightweight flexibility and lasting comfort. Uncomplicated by design, the Nelson makes a case for the kind of sneaker that never needs to chase trends.

Seiko celebrates the 50th anniversary of Steven Spielberg's 1975 film Jaws with the Prospex SRPL81, a dive watch with a shark's dorsal fin and the boat Orca from the movie engraved on the caseback. The 45mm stainless steel case is rated to 656 feet and fitted with a sapphire crystal and a deep blue silicone strap. Seiko limited the run to 5,000, each numbered on the caseback and packed in a collector's box.

entry.content:
A24's movie cat encyclopedia has more than 1,000 entries, from famous names like Puss in Boots and Austin Powers' Mr. Bigglesworth to unnamed alley cats on screen for only a few seconds. Entries run alphabetically and cover the range of roles cats have played on screen: household pets, villains, spaceship crew, cat-woman hybrids, including Holly Golightly's orange tabby from Breakfast at Tiffany's and Jones from the Alien franchise. Original essays cover recurring cat archetypes like Bad Omen Cats and Talking Cats, alongside profiles of real cat actors with their own IMDb credits. The book runs 420 pages in a buckram-wrapped hardcover, with more than 1,900 film stills throughout.

entry.summary: Lüm-Tec has built watches for the U.S. government and SWAT teams, and its own Combat B line was tested in desert heat and on frozen mountaintops. The Combat B72's 43mm stainless steel case is forged for strength, bead-blasted against scratches and coated in gunmetal. Its dial car
entry.content:
Lüm-Tec has built watches for the U.S. government and SWAT teams, and its own Combat B line was tested in desert heat and on frozen mountaintops. The Combat B72's 43mm stainless steel case is forged for strength, bead-blasted against scratches and coated in gunmetal. Its dial carries more than 30 layers of Super-Luminova, a glow-in-the-dark material, over a reflective base. A domed sapphire crystal cuts glare, and the watch is water resistant to 656 feet, with double seals at the crown and threaded caseback. Its strap lugs curve downward to wrap the wrist, so it wears smaller than it measures. Two nylon straps, in black and gray, are looped through both sides, so the watch stays on the wrist even if a spring bar, the pin holding a strap end, is damaged. Lüm-Tec replaces the battery and pressure-tests it free for life, and only 500 numbered pieces will be made worldwide.
